title: Olivia Rodrigo Shares a Sadder Side of Christmas
summary:
Olivia Rodrigo is having a very musical Christmas. Just weeks after releasing her first Christmas song, 'Take Me Home (4 Christmas),' the singer has shared its flip side: a sadder holiday ballad called 'Miss This Christmas.' The official version is now streaming exclusively on Amazon Music.
The two songs show two sides of love at Christmas. 'Take Me Home (4 Christmas)' is upbeat and full of excitement, inspired by Christmas songs from the Eighties. In it, Rodrigo sings about the thrill of meeting a boyfriend's or girlfriend's family for the holidays. Its playful video stars Saturday Night Live cast member Ben Marshall as the guy bringing her home, with Cynthia Nixon playing his mom.
'Miss This Christmas' is the opposite mood. It is a slow, melancholy ballad about missing someone during the holidays, like a Christmas card that arrives with a lump in your throat. 'Happy Christmas to the lonely / Broken hearts that feel just like me,' Rodrigo sings. She wrote the song with Dan Nigro and Amy Allen.
Rodrigo first sang the song live this week at Nashville's Bridgestone Arena, where she called it a 'really sad Christmas song' and told the crowd that 'no one's ever really heard it before.' Two days earlier, she had recorded two 20-minute sets at Jack White's Blue Room in Nashville.
It has been a big year for Rodrigo. She earned seven Grammy nominations for her album 'you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love,' including Album of the Year, Song of the Year and Record of the Year. Her Unraveled tour runs through December 20 in Las Vegas, then continues with a Los Angeles residency from January 12 through 29.
why_it_matters: Holiday songs usually celebrate only happy feelings, but many people feel lonely at Christmas, so a famous singer sharing a sad holiday song shows that those feelings are normal and worth singing about.

A ballad is a slow song that tells a story or shares a feeling, so a sad ballad can capture missing someone at Christmas.

The Grammy Awards are major music prizes, and a nomination means a singer's work has been chosen as one of the year's best.
